decision: Story and order: the Civic reel's v19 structure with the MR2's eight parts in the lookbook's partOrder (Front Bumper, Headlight Eyelids, Hood Vents, Side Skirt Fender Combo, Rear Bumper Spats, Diffuser V1+, Hardtop, Rear Duckbill), then respray, lowered suspension (Performance tab), 6-spoke wheels, exit line once, end card
why: Brief: 'the exact same thing, but for the MR2 Spyder kit'. Every one of the nineteen Civic rounds is applied from the start: each part entered from the list and left back to it, paint-matched parts, redrawn pop-up, stats panel on every part screen, plain row names, game titles kept, forward frames only.

decision: Car tag: KARIN / JASON'S '01 RUNABOUT
why: Brief asks for the GTA-universe name. Karin is the series' Toyota (official). Two web searches found no official counterpart of the MR2 Spyder / MR-S (only fan mods; the Vapid GB200 borrows from the MR2 222D rally prototype, a different car and maker); the GTA wikis themselves are not reachable from this environment, so that is 'not found', not 'proven absent'. 'Runabout' is my choice: MR stands for Midship Runabout. '01 is the model year of the game model's source (2001 MR-S S Edition). The model still wears its Toyota / MR-S badges.

decision: Prices from Epsilon-Site showroom/catalog/products.json, base variants: 900 / 100 / 400 / 700 / 350 / 750 / 50 / 220; game items 750 (suspension) and 560 (rims) as in the Civic reel; wallet starts at 4,780 and ends at 0
why: Never invent numbers. The MR2 parts are sold in fibreglass only, so unlike the Civic there is no painted-variant price: the reel shows them paint matched at the unpainted price (declared). Hood Vents uses 'Fiberglass Vents ONLY' (400): the model shows vents, not the relocation brackets (470).

decision: Hardtop charged at 50 with a PREORDER DEPOSIT badge beside EPSILON+
why: The catalogue's only figure for the hardtop is a 50 non-refundable preorder deposit; there is no price. Showing 50 unlabelled would read as the hardtop's price; leaving the hardtop out would drop the lookbook's biggest visual change. Declared to the owner.

decision: TC Wing (1,100, backorder) left out
why: It is on the kit page but not in the game model (car notes: 'Not exported: the TC wing'); nothing can be shown for it, so nothing is sold for it. Whether it can sit with the duckbill cannot be judged from this model.

decision: Colours: arrives in Silver Streak Metallic 1E7; Recommended tab lists the lookbook's eight ZZW30 paints (Silver Streak, Silver, Phantom Gray, Black, Super White II, Absolutely Red, Paradise Blue, Solar Yellow); Solar Yellow 576 is bought
why: Brief: stock colour and OEM list from the lookbook's paints, finishing on the lookbook colour. Silver shows each part's shape in the shop light and makes the yellow respray read; the list is the lookbook's, not mine.

decision: Views per part: Front Bumper and Eyelids on capture B's front-bumper camera (F), Hood Vents on its hood camera (H, new), Side Skirts on its low front-quarter screen (D), Spats and Diffuser on its exhaust camera (E), Hardtop on its rear-bed camera from behind and above (T, new), Duckbill on capture A's rear view (A)
why: Each part needs a game camera that shows it. The roof camera (B 4:44) has the game's car across two thirds of the frame, which the MR2 cannot cover; the rear-bed camera shows the whole roof from behind with the car compact in frame.

decision: Cameras re-sited for the MR2 by search (tools/camsearch.py): position, heading +-12, pitch +-3 (free for the two new views) minimising the game car's uncovered pixels plus a cost for zooming in further than needed; part bounding boxes kept clear of the option block and stats panel. Uncovered before plate: M 3.6 %, F 4.5, H 1.4, D 6.0, E 14, T 2.1, A 1.5, S 10 of the game car's mask; wheel close-up set by hand (our wheel on the game's, 22 % uncovered: the MR2's nose is far shorter)
why: The MR2 is 3.89 m against the Civic's 4.67 m and a 5.2 m game car. Knowledge doc: cover the game's car by moving the camera, do not invent and blur background. Without the zoom cost the search filled the frame with the car. Consequence, declared: the MR2 stands larger against the room than it really is.

decision: Whips: outward whips rendered (8 orbit cameras each); return whips play the outward frames backwards except after the hardtop and the wheels, which are rendered again
why: A 61 px blur hides one added part; a roof changing from black fabric to body colour, and bronze wheels, would show. Saves about 80 Blender launches.

decision: Part screens 1.8 s (54 frames), pop-up 1.07 s; shop section 36.8 s
why: Eleven purchases with every navigation step need about 37 s at the Civic's rhythm. The Honey FM clip is 28.8 s from where its music starts, so it cannot cover this section in one unbroken piece; told the owner and asked for a longer clip rather than cutting the navigation or looping music.

decision: 6-spoke wheel rebuilt from the TE37 scan (Drive 1PvGYb5luOlEnScSWFwCiPoSgtfzbYCUu) with target 400000 as the third argument; bronze #8c6b3f; body dropped 45 mm
why: wheel6_hd_scantyre.glb was not in Dropbox. The knowledge doc's command without a target simplifies the whole scan to 30k triangles first, so RIM_TRIS=160000 had no effect (14k-triangle rim); with 400000 the rim and tyre come out at 160k each. Bronze hex is my pick: the Civic log only says 'bronze'.

decision: End card: white EPSILON+ wordmark on black until the owner's palm-sunset image is supplied; no radio bed yet
why: bg_user.webp and radio.wav are not in the Dropbox folder (searched it and the whole Dropbox). Brief: do not substitute another image or other music; carry on and ask once.

decision: After the first full composite: game-car masks widened (menu view: the nose and bumper under the list; rear-bed view: roof rack, tail lights, bumper; wheel view: fender top), plates never sample the stats panel or option block, low side views continue the wall downward above the MR2's nose, rear view mirrors the booth wall in sideways, the mirrored floor of the rear-bed view is desaturated
why: Looked at one frame per purchase at delivery size: scraps of the game's car showed beside the smaller MR2 (chrome bumper by the nose, tail lights and yellow floor reflections round the tail, a mirrored stats panel, a mirrored sign above the nose). The MR2 leaves 1-9 % of the frame to fill where the Civic left 0-5 %.

decision: Titles and option blocks are laid on as layers after the car on every part screen; title lettering gets a soft dark halo only where the car is behind it
why: On the rear view the MR2's tail reaches into the title corner and its shadow dimmed the price block; the EPSILON+ badge also sat above the pasted rectangle and was lost. One rule for all part screens keeps them alike (Civic v14: 'the front bumper is also missing the stats bar').

decision: Wheel screen: wallet figure without its icon
why: The Civic's glyph cut-out of the icon assumed the game car's yellow behind it; over the MR2 it carried an orange patch. A missing icon for 2 s is the smaller fault.

decision: Whips into part screens hold the state's own title lettering mask (strokes found by top-hat), not 'bright pixels in the title corner'
why: Checked one frame of all twenty whips at delivery size: on the two whips into the rear view the car's highlight inside the title corner was held sharp as a white streak beside the title (the Civic's v15 'screen tear' class of fault).

decision: v2: the reel renders a corrected copy of the game model (tools/reel_model.py -> mr2-reel.glb, in media); the lookbook GLB in Epsilon-Site is not changed
why: Owner's v1 notes are about the model: hood not cut for the vents, fender not trimmed for the skirts, no TC wing, flat red tail lamps, exhaust through the diffuser, faceted surfaces. Fixing them in a derived file keeps the reel moving; the same faults are still in the published model and are flagged to the owner as a separate job.

decision: v2 model: every mesh welded and smooth-shaded, hard edges kept above 40 degrees
why: Owner: 'the polygon quality of the model is also visibly low'. The published GLB is unwelded, so each triangle shaded flat; the triangle count was never the problem.

decision: v2 model: hood skin inside the vents' footprint split into body_hood_cut (2,268 cm2), hidden once the vents are bought
why: Owner: 'hood needs to be cut out for the hood vents'. The vents are recessed into the hood: the stock skin lay up to 3 cm above the louvres and hid them. Cut by face centre after subdividing to 7 mm so the edge runs under the vent's rim.

decision: v2 model: front fender piece split into body_fender_cut (782 faces, both sides) from the owner's scan 'Cutted fender Piece' in the kit file, hidden once the skirts are bought; the skirt node mirrored to the right side
why: Owner: 'fender needs to be trimmed for new skirts'. The kit file holds a scan of the piece that is cut away; registered to the model at 1.8 mm median (ICP on Ducktail, Hood Vent, skirt and arch vent). The published skirt node is the left side only.

decision: v2: TC Wing added as a ninth part (kit file 'rear wing' collection: DEMO_1.006-009 + Bolt.001), satin black with chrome bolts, $1,100 from the catalogue with a BACKORDER badge, bought last on the rear view; it sits above the duckbill, so both stay on
why: Owner: 'the rear TC spoiler needs to be added'. v1 left it out because the published model lacks it. Black is my choice (an aluminium motorsport wing, and the kit file gives it its own grey material, not the body's); it can be paint matched if wanted. Wallet now 5,880 > 0.

decision: v2 model: tail pipe split off the trim; with the diffuser a copy raised 97 mm is shown instead (bottom of the pipe 12 mm above the diffuser's top surface)
why: Owner: 'the rear diffuser being added needs to change the exhaust position so it clears'. The stock pipe ran through the diffuser plate. Raised straight up, tucked behind the bumper edge; the real re-routed exhaust is not modelled anywhere I could find, so this is a placement, not the owner's part.

decision: v2 model: tail lamps get the rip's own lights texture back (lights_lod0.png from MR-S_1.blend): chrome lamp units and ribbed red lower lens opaque, the atlas's red lens with two clear windows see-through, the untextured outer cover clear
why: Owner: 'the rear tail light needs the original OEM textures put back in'. The GLB still carried the UVs but shaded every lamp face flat red. Three passes: the first only reached pieces whose first face was a lamp material (selection per connected piece), found by listing every surface in the lamp volume.

decision: v2 whips: a whip into a part screen shows the car before that purchase, the whip back shows it after; the part screen holds the 'before' state for 0.67 s (was 0.4 s)
why: Owner: 'need to start with stock bumper', 'at the 0:01 transition the aftermarket bumper flashes on the car'. v1 rendered the first whip with the new bumper already on to reuse it for the return. Whip renders are now grouped by how the car looks at that step (LOOK in renders.py).

decision: v2: list row and screens read 'Rear Diffuser' (was the catalogue's 'Diffuser V1+')
why: Owner: relabel it. Client's wording wins over the catalogue's.

decision: v2 fills: only the seam of a mirrored fill is softened (was the whole fill at 60 %); wheel close-up mirrors the real out-of-focus background up from below instead of a 14 px blur
why: Owner: 'some of the asset blurring needs to be done better / artificially filled'. Offered AI inpainting through their Higgsfield account (about 60-100 credits, uploads the game frames): declined, local only.

decision: v2 end card: the owner's palm-sunset image (bg_user.webp, from their Drive folder 'Claude training - GTA6 mod-shop reel assets', sha256 688bdc33… verified) with the white wordmark, as in the Civic v19
why: The Civic session placed the file on the owner's Drive at the owner's request; it replaces the black placeholder. Radio clip still not available.

decision: v3 radio bed: the owner's 98.5 s screen recording of a 'GTA VI Club Radio' mix, one unbroken piece from 49.65 s, so that the music's own break at 91.75 s falls on the cut to the end card; band-limited and narrowed as in the Civic reel, bed -32 dB between events, 4 dB dip under the line, quiet tail fades under the card
why: Owner supplied a longer recording after I said the 30.8 s clip could not cover a 42 s shop section. The first 31 s of the recording is a quiet build 12 dB under the rest, which would leave most of the reel with almost no radio; the loud stretch (31-91.75 s) is 60 s, enough to cover the shop unbroken. No join inside the reel: the music is already playing when the reel opens (0.5 s fade-in) and leaves on its own break. Picture identical to v2.

decision: v4: radio bed 9 dB lower (about -40 dB between events, 16 dB under the purchase sound); nothing else changed
why: Owner: 'too loud, needs to be background radio volume'. v3 matched the Civic reel's measured bed level (-32 dB), but this is a dense club track where the Civic's clip was sparse: equal RMS is not equal loudness, and I cannot hear the difference. For a dense track start well under the Civic's figure.
